title: حِكَايَةُ التَّاجِرِ وَأَوْلَادِهِ
titleEn: The Merchant and His Sons, continued
part: Night 42 · The Merchant and His Sons, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 340–344 (Night 42, continuing directly from nights-41), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 42 follows the Caliph's discovery of the sham funeral: two slave girls gossip within his hearing, and he sends Jaʿfar to seize Ghānim ibn Ayyūb and bring back Qūt al-Qulūb. Ghānim escapes in disguise with a pot of meat on his head, while the girl, left behind, is taken to the palace. Ghānim wanders, sick and starving, in a distant town, where his own mother and sister, now beggars, see him without knowing him; a Baghdad market-chief takes him in. Shahrazād is overtaken by morning. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الثَّانِيَةُ وَالْأَرْبَعُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-thāniyatu wa-al-arbaʿūna
sentences.l: And-when came-to-be the-night, the-second-one and-the-forty,
sentences.i: When the forty-second night came,

sentences.t: قٰلَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُأَنَّ الْخَلِيفَةَ لَمْ يَزَلْ يَتَرَدَّدُ عَلَى قَبْرِهَا مُدَّةَ شَهْرٍ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-khalīfata lam yazal yataraddadu ʿalā qabrihā muddata shahrin
sentences.l: She-said: It-has-reached-me, O the-king the-fortunate, that the-caliph did-not cease going-back-and-forth upon her-tomb a-period-of a-month.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the Caliph did not cease to visit her tomb for a month.
sentences.n: The print gives قلت for قالت (a slip of the pen or press; read qālat, with the dagger alif supplied). It also runs السعيد and أن together into one word, السعيدان; we split the sense but keep the printed letters, so read saʿīdu anna.

sentences.t: فَاتَّفَقَ أَنَّ الْخَلِيفَةَ دَخَلَ الْحَرِيمَ بَعْدَ انْصِرَافِ الْأُمَرَاءِ وَالْوُزَرَاءِ إِلَى بُيُوتِهِمْ فَنَامَ سَاعَةً
sentences.tr: fa-ittafaqa anna al-khalīfata dakhala al-ḥarīma baʿda inṣirāfi al-umarāʾi wa-al-wuzarāʾi ilā buyūtihim fa-nāma sāʿatan
sentences.l: And-it-so-fell-out that the-caliph entered the-harem after the-departure-of the-emirs and-the-viziers to their-houses, and-slept an-hour.
sentences.i: Now it so fell out that the Caliph went into the harem after the emirs and viziers had gone away to their houses, and he slept for an hour.

sentences.t: فَجَلَسَتْ عِنْدَ رَأْسِهِ جَارِيَةٌ تُرَوِّحُهُ بِالْمِرْوَحَةِ وَعِنْدَ رِجْلَيْهِ جَارِيَةٌ تَكْبِسُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-jalasat ʿinda raʾsihi jāriyatun turawwiḥuhu bi-al-mirwaḥati wa-ʿinda rijlayhi jāriyatun takbisuhu
sentences.l: And-sat at his-head a-girl fanning-him with-the-fan, and-at his-two-feet a-girl kneading-him.
sentences.i: and by his head sat a girl who fanned him with a fan, and at his feet another who kneaded his limbs.
sentences.n: تكبسه: kabasa is to press or knead; here it means massaging the sleeper's legs and feet. The shadda on تروّحه is the edition's own and is kept.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَامَ وَانْتَبَهَ وَفَتَحَ عَيْنَيْهِ وَغَمَّضَهُمَا فَسَمِعَ الْجَارِيَةَ الَّتِي عِنْدَ رَأْسِهِ تَقُولُ لِلَّتِي عِنْدَ رِجْلَيْهِ وَيْلَكِ يَاخَيْزُرَانُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā nāma wa-intabaha wa-fataḥa ʿaynayhi wa-ghammaḍahumā fa-samiʿa al-jāriyata al-latī ʿinda raʾsihi taqūlu li-al-latī ʿinda rijlayhi waylaki yā Khayzurānu
sentences.l: And-when he-slept and-awoke and-opened his-two-eyes and-shut-them, he-heard the-girl who at his-head saying to-the-one-who at his-two-feet: Woe-to-you, O-Khayzurān!
sentences.i: When he had slept, and woken, and opened his eyes and closed them again, he heard the girl at his head say to the girl at his feet: Come now, Khayzurān!
sentences.n: He wakes, opens his eyes, and shuts them again: he lies still and feigns sleep so as to overhear. The girls' names are Khayzurān (the one at his feet) and Qaḍīb al-Bān (the one at his head). ويلك is literally 'woe to you', but as an address between friends it only calls for attention. ياخيزران is printed as one word, yā Khayzurān.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ لَهَا نَعَمْ يَا قَضِيبَ الْبَانِ
sentences.tr: qālat lahā naʿam yā qaḍība al-bāni
sentences.l: She-said to-her: Yes, O twig-of the-moringa-tree.
sentences.i: She answered: Yes, Qaḍīb al-Bān.
sentences.n: The speaker changes without warning: this is Khayzurān replying. قضيب البان, 'branch of the bān-tree', is a name given to a slender girl; the bān is the moringa, a tree proverbial for its supple, slender boughs.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ لَهَا إِنَّ سَيِّدَنَا لَيْسَ عِنْدَةُ عِلْمٌ بِمَا جَرَى وَأَنَّهُ يَسْهَرُ عَلَى قَبْرٍ لَمْ يَكُنْ فِيهِ إِلَّاخَشَبَةٌ مُنَجَّرَةٌ صَنْعَةَ النَّجَّارِ
sentences.tr: qālat lahā inna sayyidanā laysa ʿindahu ʿilmun bi-mā jarā wa-annahu yashharu ʿalā qabrin lam yakun fīhi illā khashabatun munajjaratun ṣanʿata al-najjāri
sentences.l: She-said to-her: Indeed our-lord, not-is at-him knowledge of-what happened, and-that-he keeps-vigil over a-tomb not was in-it except a-plank, planed, the-craft-of the-carpenter.
sentences.i: She said to her: Our lord knows nothing of what has happened, and he keeps vigil over a tomb in which there is nothing but a plank of wood, the carpenter's handiwork.
sentences.n: Qaḍīb al-Bān speaks again. عندة is a print slip for عنده; the final letter is left unpointed here, read ʿindahu. إلاخشبة is printed as one word, illā khashabatan, 'except a plank'. منجرة is read munajjara, 'planed, hewn' (najjara, to work wood); if the print is corrupt for منحوتة 'carved' the sense is much the same.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهَا الْأُخْرَى وَقُوتُ الْقُلُوبِ أَىُّ شَيْءٍ أَصَابَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahā al-ukhrā wa-qūtu al-qulūbi ayyu shayʾin aṣābahā
sentences.l: And-said to-her the-other: And-Qūt al-Qulūb — which thing befell-her?
sentences.i: The other said to her: And Qūt al-Qulūb, what has befallen her?
sentences.n: اى is the print's spelling of أي (final yāʾ written dotless, like الاخرى and فى elsewhere); read ayyu.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ اعْلَمِي
sentences.tr: fa-qālat iʿlamī
sentences.l: And-she-said: Know!
sentences.i: Then she said: Know this,
sentences.n: The speech continues in the next unit.

sentences.t: أَنَّ السِّتَّ زُبَيْدَةَ أَرْسَلَتْ مَعَ جَارِيَةٍ قُرْصَ بَنْجٍ وَبَنَّجَتْهَا فَلَمَّا تَحَكَّمَ الْبَنْجُ مِنْهَا جَعَلَتْهَا فِي صُنْدُوقٍ وَأَرْسَلَتْهَا مَعَ صَوَابٍ وَكَافُورٍ وَأَمَرَتْهُمَا أَنْ يَرْمِيَاهَا فِى التُّرْبَةِ
sentences.tr: anna al-sitta Zubaydata arsalat maʿa jāriyatin qurṣa banjin wa-bannajathā fa-lammā taḥakkama al-banju minhā jaʿalathā fī ṣundūqin wa-arsalathā maʿa Ṣawābin wa-Kāfūrin wa-amarathumā an yarmiyāhā fī al-turbati
sentences.l: that the-lady Zubayda sent with a-girl a-disc-of bhang and-drugged-her; and-when the-bhang took-mastery of-her, she-put-her in a-chest and-sent-her with Ṣawāb and-Kāfūr, and-commanded-them-two that they-two-throw-her in the-burial-ground.
sentences.i: that the Lady Zubayda sent a girl with a pill of bhang and drugged her; and when the drug had mastered her, she laid her in a chest and sent her off with Ṣawāb and Kāfūr, bidding them cast her into the burial-ground.
sentences.n: بنج (Persian bang) is henbane or hemp, a narcotic; بنّجها is 'she drugged her'. Ṣawāb and Kāfūr are two palace servants (eunuchs). Note the dotless yāʾ in فى. The dual يرمياها loses its final nūn after أن.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ خَيْزُرَانُ وَيْلَكِ يَا قَضِيبَ الْبَانِ هَلِ السِّتُّ قُوتُ الْقُلُوبِ مَا مَاتَتْ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat Khayzurānu waylaki yā qaḍība al-bāni hali al-sittu qūtu al-qulūbi mā mātat
sentences.l: And-said Khayzurān: Woe-to-you, O twig-of the-moringa, is-it-that the-lady Qūt al-Qulūb did-not die?
sentences.i: Then Khayzurān said: Come now, Qaḍīb al-Bān, has Lady Qūt al-Qulūb not died, then?
sentences.n: ما ماتت: Middle Arabic uses mā with the perfect to negate a past event, where Classical Arabic would say lam tamut. Combined with هل it makes a question expecting the answer 'surely she is dead'.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَا وَاللَّهِ سَلَامَةُ شَبَابِهَا مِنَ الْمَوْتِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lā wa-allāhi salāmatu shabābihā mina al-mawti
sentences.l: And-she-said: No, by-God — safety-of her-youth from the-death.
sentences.i: She said: No, by God! Her youth is safe from death.
sentences.n: سلامة شبابها من الموت has no verb: it is an exclamation, 'safe is her youth from death', or perhaps an oath-like wish, 'by the safety of her youth'.

sentences.t: وَلَكِنْ أَنَا سَمِعْتُ السِّتَّ زُبَيْدَةَ تَقُولُ
sentences.tr: wa-lākin anā samiʿtu al-sitta Zubaydata taqūlu
sentences.l: But I heard the-lady Zubayda saying
sentences.i: But I have heard Lady Zubayda say
sentences.n: What Zubayda said follows in the next two units.

sentences.t: أَنَّ قُوتَ الْقُلُوبِ عِنْدَ شَابٍّ تَاجِرٍ اسْمُهُ غَانِمُ بْنُ أَيُّوبَ الدِّمَشْقِيُّ
sentences.tr: anna qūta al-qulūbi ʿinda shābbin tājirin ismuhu Ghānimu ibnu Ayyūba al-Dimashqīyu
sentences.l: that Qūt al-Qulūb is with a-young-man, a-merchant, his-name Ghānim son-of Ayyūb the-Damascene,
sentences.i: that Qūt al-Qulūb is with a young merchant whose name is Ghānim son of Ayyūb, the Damascene,

sentences.t: وَأَنَّ لَهَا عِنْدَهُ بِهَٰذَا الْيَوْمِ أَرْبَعَ شُهُورٍ
sentences.tr: wa-anna lahā ʿindahu bi-hādhā al-yawmi arbaʿa shuhūrin
sentences.l: and-that for-her at-him, as-of this the-day, four months.
sentences.i: and that she has been with him four months to this very day.
sentences.n: Here the noun phrase اربع شهور is the subject of أنّ, and لها عنده 'she has with him' is placed before it. Four is printed without tāʾ marbūṭa (arbaʿ shuhūr) where Classical Arabic wants arbaʿat shuhūr; Middle Arabic often ignores the reversed gender of numbers.

sentences.t: وَسَيِّدُنَا هَٰذَا يَبْكِي وَيَسْهَرُ اللَّيَالِيَ عَلَى قَبْرٍ لَمْ يَكُنْ فِيهِ مَيِّتٌ
sentences.tr: wa-sayyidunā hādhā yabkī wa-yashharu al-layāliya ʿalā qabrin lam yakun fīhi mayyitun
sentences.l: and-our-lord this-one weeps and-keeps-vigil the-nights over a-tomb not was in-it a-dead-one.
sentences.i: while this lord of ours weeps and keeps vigil night after night over a tomb with no dead body in it.

sentences.t: وَصَارَتَا تَتَحَدَّثَانِ بِهَٰذَا الْحَدِيثِ وَالْخَلِيفَةُ يَسْمَعُ كَلَامَهُمَا
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāratā tataḥaddathāni bi-hādhā al-ḥadīthi wa-al-khalīfatu yasmaʿu kalāmahumā
sentences.l: And-the-two-became conversing with-this the-talk, while the-caliph hears their-two-speech.
sentences.i: And the two went on talking in this fashion while the Caliph listened to their words.
sentences.n: Narrative resumes. ṣāra with a verb, 'they came to be talking', is a common way to say 'they went on'.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ الْجَارِيَتَانِ مِنَ الْحَدِيثِ وَعَرَفَ الْقَضِيَّةَ وَأَنَّ هَٰذَا الْقَبْرَ زُورٌ وَمُحَالٌ وَأَنَّ قُوتَ الْقُلُوبِ عِنْدَ غَانِمِ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ مُدَّةَ أَرْبَعَةِ أَشْهُرٍ غَضِبَ الْخَلِيفَةُ غَضَبًا شَدِيدًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha al-jāriyatāni mina al-ḥadīthi wa-ʿarafa al-qaḍiyyata wa-anna hādhā al-qabra zūrun wa-muḥālun wa-anna qūta al-qulūbi ʿinda Ghānimi ibni Ayyūba muddata arbaʿati ashhurin ghaḍiba al-khalīfatu ghaḍaban shadīdan
sentences.l: And-when finished the-two-girls from the-talk, and-he-knew the-affair, and-that this the-tomb is a-falsehood and-an-absurdity, and-that Qūt al-Qulūb is with Ghānim son-of Ayyūb a-period-of four months, grew-angry the-caliph an-anger severe.
sentences.i: When the two girls had finished their talk, and he had grasped the whole affair, that this tomb was a falsehood and a farce, and that Qūt al-Qulūb had been four months with Ghānim son of Ayyūb, the Caliph was seized with a violent rage.
sentences.n: The subject of عرف is the Caliph, not the girls; he is named only in the main clause, غضب الخليفة, which closes the long lammā-clause. The verb فرغ stays singular before its dual subject, as Classical Arabic requires.

sentences.t: وَقَامَ وَدَخَلَ عَلَى أُمَرَاءِ دَوْلَتِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāma wa-dakhala ʿalā umarāʾi dawlatihi
sentences.l: and-rose and-entered upon the-emirs-of his-regime.
sentences.i: He rose and went in to the emirs of his court.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذٰلِكَ أَقْبَلَ الْوَزِيرُ جَعْفَرٌ الْبَرْ مَكِيُّ وَقَبَّلَ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika aqbala al-wazīru Jaʿfarun al-Bar Makīyu wa-qabbala al-arḍa bayna yadayhi
sentences.l: And-at that came-forward the-vizier Jaʿfar the-Bar-Makī and-kissed the-earth between his-two-hands.
sentences.i: Thereupon the vizier Jaʿfar the Barmakid came forward and kissed the ground before him.
sentences.n: البر مكي is printed as two words; it is al-Barmakī, 'of the Barmakid house'. Kissing the ground is the courtier's homage before the sovereign; بين يديه, 'between his two hands', means 'before him'.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْخَلِيفَةُ بِغَيْظٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-khalīfatu bi-ghayẓin
sentences.l: And-said to-him the-caliph with-rage:
sentences.i: And the Caliph said to him in fury:

sentences.t: انْزِلْ يَاجَعْفَرُ بِجَمَاعَةٍ وَاسْأَلْ عَنْ بَيْتِ غَانِمِ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ
sentences.tr: inzil yā Jaʿfaru bi-jamāʿatin wa-isʾal ʿan bayti Ghānimi ibni Ayyūba
sentences.l: Go-down, O-Jaʿfar, with-a-company, and-ask about the-house-of Ghānim son-of Ayyūb,
sentences.i: Go down, Jaʿfar, with a company of men, and ask after the house of Ghānim son of Ayyūb,
sentences.n: يا جعفر is printed as one word. 'Go down' means go down from the palace into the city.

sentences.t: وَاكْبِسُوا دَارَهُ وَايْتُونِي بِجَارِبَتِي قُوتِ الْقُلُوبِ
sentences.tr: wa-ikbisū dārahu wa-ʾtūnī bi-jāriyatī qūti al-qulūbi
sentences.l: and-raid his-house and-bring-me with-my-girl Qūt al-Qulūb,
sentences.i: and raid his house, and bring me my slave-girl Qūt al-Qulūb,
sentences.n: وايتوني is the imperative 'bring me' (wa-ʾtūnī); the yāʾ is only the written seat of the hamza, so it is left with a sukūn. In بجاربتي the printed ب is a slip for ي (read bi-jāriyatī, 'with my slave-girl'), so that letter is left unpointed. Verbs of 'bringing' take بـ for the thing brought.

sentences.t: وَلَا بُدَّلِي أَنْ أُعَذِّبَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-lā buddalī an uʿadhdhibahu
sentences.l: and-no escape-for-me that I-torment-him.
sentences.i: for I must punish him.
sentences.n: ولا بدلي is printed with لي attached to بد: lā budda lī, 'there is no escape for me from', that is, 'I must'. أعذبه may be 'torture' or simply 'punish'.

sentences.t: فَأَجَابَهُ جَعْفَرٌ بِالسَّمْعِ وَالطَّاعَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-ajābahu Jaʿfarun bi-al-samʿi wa-al-ṭāʿati
sentences.l: And-answered-him Jaʿfar with-the-hearing and-the-obedience.
sentences.i: Jaʿfar answered him with hearing and obedience.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذٰلِكَ نَزَلَ جَعْفَرٌ وَالْخَلْقُ وَالْعَالَمُ وَالْوَالِي صُحْبَتَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika nazala Jaʿfarun wa-al-khalqu wa-al-ʿālamu wa-al-wālī ṣuḥbatahu
sentences.l: And-at that went-down Jaʿfar and-the-creation and-the-world and-the-governor, his-company.
sentences.i: Thereupon Jaʿfar went down, with a throng of people and the city governor in his train.
sentences.n: الخلق والعالم, 'the creation and the world', is a doubled phrase for a great crowd. صحبته, 'in his company', is accusative of accompaniment.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَالُوا سَائِرِينَ إِلَى أَنْ أَتَوْا إِلَى دَارِ غَانِمٍ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazālū sāʾirīna ilā an atawā ilā dāri Ghānimin
sentences.l: and-did-not cease travelling until they-came to the-house-of Ghānim.
sentences.i: and they rode steadily on until they came to Ghānim's house.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ غَانِمُ بْنُ أَيُّوبَ خَرَجَ فِي ذٰلِكَ الْوَقْتِ وَجَاءَ بِقِدْرَةِ لَحْمٍ وَأَرَادَأَنْ يَمُدَّيَدَهُ لِيَأْكُلَ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna Ghānimu ibnu Ayyūba kharaja fī dhālika al-waqti wa-jāʾa bi-qidrati laḥmin wa-arāda an yamudda yadahu li-yaʾkula
sentences.l: And-was Ghānim son-of Ayyūb had-gone-out at that the-time, and-came with-a-pot-of meat, and-wished that-he-extend his-hand in-order-to-eat.
sentences.i: Now Ghānim son of Ayyūb had gone out at that very hour and come back with a pot of meat, and was just reaching out his hand to eat.
sentences.n: This sentence breaks off at the edge of the slice and continues in the next one. وارادان and يمديده are each printed as one word (wa-arāda an, yamudda yadahu). قدرة is read qidra, a small cooking-pot; it could also be read as qudra, 'power', but the sense of meat in a pot rules that out.

sentences.t: مِنْهَا هُوَ وَقُوتُ الْقُلُوبِ
sentences.tr: minhā huwa wa-Qūtu al-Qulūbi
sentences.l: from-her/it, he and-Qūt al-Qulūb
sentences.i: …from it, he and Qūt al-Qulūb,
sentences.n: The slice opens mid-sentence: this fragment continues from the neighbouring slice before it (something like “… [eating] from it, he and Qūt al-Qulūb, when …”). Qūt al-Qulūb, “Sustenance of Hearts”, is the girl’s name; huwa is Ghānim.

sentences.t: فَلَاحَتْ مِنْهَا الْتِفَاتَةٌ فَوَجَدَتِ الْبَلَاءَ أَحَاطَ بِالدَّارِ مِنْ كُلِّ جَانِبٍ
sentences.tr: fa-lāḥat minhā iltifātatun fa-wajadati al-balāʾa aḥāṭa bi-al-dāri min kulli jānibin
sentences.l: So-flashed from-her a-glance, and-she-found the-calamity had-encircled the-house from every side,
sentences.i: A glance of hers happened to flash out, and she found that calamity had encircled the house on every side,
sentences.n: وجدت البلاء أحاط has no linking word: “she found the calamity (had) surrounded …”. Read it as “found that calamity had surrounded”.

sentences.t: وَالْوَزِيرُ وَالْوَالِي وَالظَّلَمَةُ وَالْمَمَالِيكُ بِسُيُوفٍ مَسْلُولَةٍ مُجَرَّدَةٍ وَقَدْ دَارُوا بِهِ كَمَا يَدُورُ بَيَاضُ الْعَيْنِ بِالسَّوَادِ
sentences.tr: wa-al-wazīru wa-al-wālī wa-al-ẓalamatu wa-al-mamālīku bi-suyūfin maslūlatin mujarradatin wa-qad dārū bihi kamā yadūru bayāḍu al-ʿayni bi-al-sawādi
sentences.l: and-the-vizier and-the-governor and-the-oppressors and-the-mamluks with-swords drawn bared, and-already they-circled around-it as circles whiteness-of the-eye around-the-blackness.
sentences.i: the vizier, the governor, the officers of oppression and the mamluks, with swords drawn and bared, having ringed it round as the white of the eye rings the black.
sentences.n: This is a circumstantial clause (“with the vizier … there”) hanging on the previous sentence. الظلمة (al-ẓalama) is literally “the wrongdoers”, i.e. the oppressive henchmen of the law. به is masculine, though الدار is feminine; it refers to the house taken as a building (or to the calamity).

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ عَرَفَتْ أَنَّ خَبَرَهَا وَصَلَ إِلَى الْخَلِيفَةِ سَيِّدِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika ʿarafat anna khabarahā waṣala ilā al-khalīfati sayyidihā
sentences.l: So at that she-knew that news-of-her had-reached to the-caliph, her-master,
sentences.i: Then she knew that word of her had reached the Caliph, her master,

sentences.t: فَأَيْقَنَتْ بِالْهَلَاكِ وَاصْفَرَّ لَوْنُهَا وَتَغَيَّرَتْ مَحَاسِنُهَا
sentences.tr: fa-ayqanat bi-al-halāki wa-iṣfarra lawnuhā wa-taghayyarat maḥāsinuhā
sentences.l: and-she-was-certain of-the-perdition, and-yellowed her-colour, and-changed her-fair-features.
sentences.i: and was certain of destruction; her colour turned sallow and her lovely features were altered.
sentences.n: أيقن بـ (ayqana bi-) “be certain of” takes its object with bi-.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ نَظَرَتْ إِلَى غَانِمٍ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ يَا حَبِيبِي فُزْ بِنَفْسِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika naẓarat ilā Ghānimin wa-qālat lahu yā ḥabībī fuz bi-nafsika
sentences.l: So at that she-looked at Ghānim and-said to-him: O my-beloved, win with-your-self!
sentences.i: Then she looked at Ghānim and said to him: Beloved, save yourself!
sentences.n: فز بنفسك, “win with your self”, is an idiom for “escape with your life”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا كَيْفَ أَعْمَلُ وَإِلَى أَيْنَ أَذْهَبُ وَمَالِي وَرِزْقِي فِي هَذِهِ الدَّارِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā kayfa aʿmalu wa-ilā ayna adhhabu wa-mālī wa-rizqī fī hādhihi al-dāri
sentences.l: So-he-said to-her: How shall-I-act, and-to where shall-I-go, and-my-wealth and-my-provision in this the-house?
sentences.i: He said to her: What am I to do, and where am I to go, with my wealth and my livelihood in this house?

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ لَاتَمْكُثْ لِئَلَّا تَهْلِكَ وَيَذْهَبَ مَالُكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu lā tamkuth li-allā tahlika wa-yadhhaba māluka
sentences.l: So-she-said to-him: Do-not-linger, lest you-perish and-go-away your-wealth.
sentences.i: She said to him: Do not tarry, lest you perish and your wealth be lost.
sentences.n: The print joins لا and the verb: لاتمكث. After لئلا (li-allā, “lest”) both verbs are subjunctive.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا يَاحَبِيبَتِي وَنُورَ عَيْنِي كَيْفَ أَصْنَعُ فِي الْخُرُوجِ وَقَدْ أَحَاطُوا بِالدَّارِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā yāḥabībatī wa-nūra ʿaynī kayfa aṣnaʿu fī al-khurūji wa-qad aḥāṭū bi-al-dāri
sentences.l: So-he-said to-her: O-my-beloved and-light-of my-eye, how shall-I-do in the-going-out, when-already they-have-encircled the-house?
sentences.i: He said to her: My beloved, light of my eyes, how am I to get out, when they have ringed the house round?
sentences.n: The print joins the vocative to the noun: ياحبيبتي (yā-ḥabībatī).

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ لَاتَخَفْ وَقَلَعَتْهُ مِنْ ثِيَابِهِ وَأَلْبَسَتْهُ ثِيَابًا بَالِيَةً
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu lā takhaf wa-qalaʿathu min thiyābihi wa-albasathu thiyāban bāliyatan
sentences.l: So-she-said to-him: Do-not-fear! And-she-stripped-him from his-clothes and-clothed-him garments worn-out.
sentences.i: She said to him: Fear not. And she stripped him of his clothes and dressed him in worn old rags.

sentences.t: وَجَاءَتْ بِالْقِدْرَةِ الَّتِي كَانَ فِيهَا اللَّحْمُ وَوَضَعَتْهَا عَلَى رَأْسِهِ وَحَطَّتْ فِي حَوَالِيهَا كِسْرَةَ خُبْزٍ وَزُبْدِيَّةَ طَعَامٍ وَوَضَعَتْهُمْ فِي مِقْطَفٍ
sentences.tr: wa-jāʾat bi-al-qidrati allatī kāna fīhā al-laḥmu wa-waḍaʿathā ʿalā raʾsihi wa-ḥaṭṭat fī ḥawālīhā kisrata khubzin wa-zubdiyyata ṭaʿāmin wa-waḍaʿathum fī miqṭafin
sentences.l: And-she-came with-the-pot in-which was in-it the-meat, and-put-it on his-head, and-set in its-surroundings a-morsel-of bread and-a-bowl-of food, and-put-them in a-basket.
sentences.i: Then she fetched the pot in which the meat had been and set it on his head; she placed around it a crust of bread and a bowl of food, and put them all into a basket.
sentences.n: قدرة (qidra) is the pot; Classical has قِدْر (qidr) without the feminine ending. حواليها for Classical حَوَالَيْهَا (ḥawālayhā), “around it”, and ووضعتهم “and she put them” (a masculine plural pronoun for things) are Middle Arabic. The basket is said to hold the pot, bread and bowl together.

sentences.t: وَقَٰلَتْ لَهُ اخْرُجْ بِهَذِهِ الْحِيلَةِ وَلَا عَلَيْكَ مِنِّي فَأَنَا أَعْرِفُ أَيَّ شَيٍّ فِي يَدِي مِنَ الْخَلِيفَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat lahu ukhruj bi-hādhihi al-ḥīlati wa-lā ʿalayka minnī fa-anā aʿrifu ayya shayyin fī yadī mina al-khalīfati
sentences.l: And-she-said to-him: Go-out by-this the-ruse, and-no upon-you from-me, for-I know what-thing is in my-hand from the-caliph.
sentences.i: And she said to him: Go out by this trick, and do not trouble yourself over me, for I know what I hold in hand to deal with the Caliph.
sentences.n: The print has قلت (“I said / you said”) for قالت; read qālat, “she said”, and the dagger alif marks it. شي is the colloquial shayy for شيء. The last clause is compressed and I am not certain of it: literally “what thing is in my hand from the Caliph”, taken here as “what means I have to deal with the Caliph”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ غَانِمٌ كَلَامَ قُوتِ الْقُلُوبِ وَمَا أَشَارَتْ بِهِ عَلَيْهِ خَرَجَ مِنْ بَيْنِهِمْ وَهُوَ حَامِلٌ الْمِقْطَفَ بِمَافِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa Ghānimun kalāma Qūti al-Qulūbi wa-mā ashārat bihi ʿalayhi kharaja min baynihim wa-huwa ḥāmilun al-miqṭafa bi-mā fīhi
sentences.l: And-when heard Ghānim the-speech-of Qūt al-Qulūb and-what she-signalled with-it upon-him, he-went-out from among-them while-he carrying the-basket with-what in-it.
sentences.i: When Ghānim heard Qūt al-Qulūb’s words and what she counselled him, he walked out from among them, carrying the basket and all that was in it,
sentences.n: أشار على (ashāra ʿalā) is “to advise someone”, with the advice introduced by bi-. The print joins بمافيه (bi-mā fīhi, “with what is in it”).

sentences.t: وَسَتَرَ عَلَيْهِ السَّتَّارُ وَنَجَامِنَ الْمَكَائِدِ وَالْإِضْرَارِ بِبَرَكَةِ نِيَّتِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-satara ʿalayhi al-sattāru wa-najā mina al-makāʾidi wa-al-iḍrāri bi-barakati niyyatihi
sentences.l: and-concealed upon-him the-Concealer, and-escaped from the-plots and-the-harmings by-blessing-of his-intention.
sentences.i: and the All-Concealing screened him, and he escaped plots and harm by the blessing of his good intent.
sentences.n: الستار (al-sattār, “the Concealer”) is a name of God. The print joins ونجا and من: ونجامن.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا وَصَلَ الْوَزِيرُ جَعْفَرٌ إِلَى نَاحِيَةِ الدَّارِ تَرَجَّلَ عَنْ حِصَانِهِ وَدَخَلَ الْبَيْتَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā waṣala al-wazīru Jaʿfarun ilā nāḥiyati al-dāri tarajjala ʿan ḥiṣānihi wa-dakhala al-bayta
sentences.l: And-when arrived the-vizier Jaʿfar at side-of the-house, he-dismounted from his-horse and-entered the-house.
sentences.i: When the vizier Jaʿfar reached the side of the house, he dismounted from his horse and went into the house,

sentences.t: وَنَظَرَ إِلَى قُوتِ الْقُلُوبِ وَقَدْ تَزَيَّنَتْ وَتَبَهْرَجَتْ وَعَبَّتْ صُنْدُوقًا مِنَ الذَّهَبِ وَالْمَصَاغِ وَالْجَوَاهِرِ وَالتُّحَفِ مِمَّاخَفَّ حَمْلُهُ وَغَلَا ثَمَنُهُ
sentences.tr: wa-naẓara ilā Qūti al-Qulūbi wa-qad tazayyanat wa-tabahrajat wa-ʿabbat ṣundūqan mina al-dhahabi wa-al-maṣāghi wa-al-jawāhiri wa-al-tuḥafi mimmā khaffa ḥamluhu wa-ghalā thamanuhu
sentences.l: and-looked at Qūt al-Qulūb, and-already she-adorned-herself and-decked-herself-out and-packed a-chest of the-gold and-the-jewellery and-the-gems and-the-rarities, of-what light its-carrying and-dear its-price.
sentences.i: and saw Qūt al-Qulūb adorned and decked out, and she had packed a chest with gold, jewellery, gems and rarities, of the kind that are light to carry and dear in price.
sentences.n: The print has عبت (ʿabbat) without the hamza: Classical عَبَّأَتْ (ʿabbaʾat), “she packed”. The print joins مماخف (mimmā khaffa, “of what is light”).

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا دَخَلَ عَلَيْهَا جَعْفَرٌ وَرَآهَا قَامَتْ عَلَى قَدَمَيْهَا وَقَبَّلَتِ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَقَٰلَتْ لَهُ يَا سَيِّدِي جَرَى الْقَلَمُ مِنَ الْقِدَمِ بِمَا حَكَمَ اللَّهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dakhala ʿalayhā Jaʿfarun wa-raʾāhā qāmat ʿalā qadamayhā wa-qabbalat al-arḍa bayna yadayhi wa-qālat lahu yā sayyidī jarā al-qalamu mina al-qidami bi-mā ḥakama Allāhu
sentences.l: And-when entered upon-her Jaʿfar and-saw-her, she-stood on her-two-feet and-kissed the-earth between his-two-hands and-said to-him: O my-master, the-pen has-run from the-eternity by-what God-decreed.
sentences.i: When Jaʿfar came in to her and saw her, she rose to her feet, kissed the ground before him, and said to him: My lord, the pen has run since eternity with what God decreed.
sentences.n: قلت for قالت again (read qālat). جرى القلم من القدم is a set phrase: the pen of destiny wrote it from eternity, i.e. “it is fated”. بين يديه (“between his two hands”) means “in his presence”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَى ذَلِكَ جَعْفَرٌ قَالَ لَهَا وَاللَّهِ يَاسِتِّي إِنَّهُ مَا أَوْصَانِي إِلَّا بِقَبْضِ غَانِمِ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾā dhālika Jaʿfarun qāla lahā wa-Allāhi yāsittī innahu mā awṣānī illā bi-qabḍi Ghānimi ibni Ayyūba
sentences.l: And-when saw that Jaʿfar, he-said to-her: By-God, O-my-lady, indeed-he did-not charge-me except with-seizing-of Ghānim son-of Ayyūb.
sentences.i: When Jaʿfar saw this, he said to her: By God, my lady, he charged me with nothing but the seizing of Ghānim son of Ayyūb.
sentences.n: ياستي is yā-sitt-ī, “my lady” (sitt is the everyday form of sayyida). إنه here is only an introductory “indeed”, and “he” is the Caliph, left unnamed. أوصى بـ is “to charge someone with something”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ يَا سَيِّدِي إِنَّهُ عَبَّى تِجَارَاتٍ وَذَهَبَ بِهَا إِلَى دِمَشْقَ وَلَا عِلْمَ لِي بِخَبَرِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat yā sayyidī innahu ʿabbā tijārātin wa-dhahaba bihā ilā Dimashqa wa-lā ʿilma lī bi-khabarihi
sentences.l: So-she-said: O my-master, indeed-he packed trade-goods and-went with-them to Damascus, and-no knowledge for-me of-his-news.
sentences.i: She said: My lord, he packed up merchandise and went off with it to Damascus, and I have no knowledge of his news.
sentences.n: عبى is the Middle Arabic form of عَبَّأَ (“to pack”), with the hamza dissolved into a final yā; compare عبت above.

sentences.t: وَأُرِيدُأَنْ تَحْفَظَ لِي هَذَا الصُّنْدُوقَ وَاحْمِلْهُ إِلَى أَنْ تُسَلِّمَهُ لِي فِي قَصْرِ أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ
sentences.tr: wa-urīdu an taḥfaẓa lī hādhā al-ṣundūqa wa-iḥmilhu ilā an tusallimahu lī fī qaṣri amīri al-muʾminīna
sentences.l: And-I-want that you-keep for-me this the-chest, and-carry-it until you-hand-it-over to-me in palace-of commander-of the-believers.
sentences.i: I would have you keep this chest for me, and carry it with you until you hand it back to me in the palace of the Commander of the Faithful.
sentences.n: The print joins واريدان (wa-urīdu an). واحمله can also be read wa-aḥmiluhu, “and I shall carry it”; the imperative “and carry it” suits the sense better, and that is how it is pointed here.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ جَعْفَرٌ السَّمْعُ وَالطَّاعَةُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Jaʿfarun al-samʿu wa-al-ṭāʿatu
sentences.l: So-said Jaʿfar: The-hearing and-the-obedience.
sentences.i: Jaʿfar said: With hearing and obedience.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَخَذَ الصُّنْدُوقَ وَأَمَرَ بِحَمْلِهِ وَقُوتُ الْقُلُوبِ مَعَهُمْ
sentences.tr: thumma akhadha al-ṣundūqa wa-amara bi-ḥamlihi wa-Qūtu al-Qulūbi maʿahum
sentences.l: Then he-took the-chest and-commanded with-carrying-it, and-Qūt al-Qulūb with-them.
sentences.i: Then he took the chest and ordered it carried off, with Qūt al-Qulūb along with them
sentences.n: The slice ends here, mid-sentence; the sentence continues in the neighbouring slice after this one. The clause “Qūt al-Qulūb with them” is circumstantial.

sentences.t: إِلَى دَارِ الْخِلَافَةِ وَهِيَ مُكَرَّمَةٌ مُعَزَّزَةٌ
sentences.tr: ilā dāri al-khilāfati wa-hiya mukarramatun muʿazzazatun
sentences.l: To abode-of the-caliphate, and-she honoured, esteemed,
sentences.i: … to the Abode of the Caliphate, honoured and esteemed.
sentences.n: This slice opens mid-sentence: the sentence began in the preceding slice, and this fragment is its end. The subject of the arrival is presumably Qūt al-Qulūb, hence the feminine mukarrama, muʿazzaza.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ هَذَا بَعْدَ أَنْ نَهَبُوا دَارَ غَانِمٍ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna hādhā baʿda an nahabū dāra Ghānimin
sentences.l: And-was this after that they-plundered house-of Ghānim.
sentences.i: All this happened after they had plundered Ghānim's house.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تَوَجَّهُوا إِلَى الْخَلِيفَةِ وَحَكَى جَعْفَرٌ لِلْخَلِيفَةِ جَمِيعَ مَاجَرَى
sentences.tr: thumma tawajjahū ilā al-khalīfati wa-ḥakā Jaʿfarun li-al-khalīfati jamīʿa mājarā
sentences.l: Then they-turned-themselves to the-caliph, and-related Jaʿfar to-the-caliph all-of what-happened.
sentences.i: Then they went before the Caliph, and Jaʿfar told the Caliph all that had happened.
sentences.n: The print runs مَا and جرى together: mā jarā, “what happened”.

sentences.t: فَأَمَرَ الْخَلِيفَةُ لِقُوتِ الْقُلُوبِ بِمَكَانٍ مُظْلِمٍ وَأَسْكَنَهَا فِيهِ وَأَلْزَمَ بِهَا عَجُوزًا لِقَضَاءِ حَاجَتِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-amara al-khalīfatu li-Qūti al-Qulūbi bi-makānin muẓlimin wa-askanahā fīhi wa-alzama bihā ʿajūzan li-qaḍāʾi ḥājatihā
sentences.l: So-ordered the-caliph for-Qūt al-Qulūb [with] a-place dark, and-lodged-her in-it, and-made-cleave to-her an-old-woman for-the-accomplishing-of her-need.
sentences.i: The Caliph ordered a dark chamber for Qūt al-Qulūb and had her lodged there, and he set an old woman over her to attend to her needs.
sentences.n: Here amara is followed by both li- (for whom) and bi- (what is ordered): “ordered, for her, a place”. Qūt al-Qulūb means “Nourishment of Hearts”. Alzama bi-hā is “assigned to her”.

sentences.t: لِأَنَّهُ ظَنَّ أَنَّ غَانِمًا قَدْ فَسَقَ بِهَا وَرَاقَدَهَا
sentences.tr: li-annahu ẓanna anna Ghāniman qad fasaqa bihā wa-rāqadahā
sentences.l: Because-that-he thought that Ghānim had committed-debauchery with-her and-lain-with-her.
sentences.i: For he supposed that Ghānim had debauched her and lain with her.
sentences.n: Rāqada is form III of raqada, “to lie down, sleep”: “to bed (someone)”, a frank euphemism the text uses plainly. Fasaqa bi-hā is “fornicated with her”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ كَتَبَ مَرْسُومًا لِلْأَمِيرِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ الزَّيْنِيِّ وَكَانَ نَائِبًا فِي دِمَشْقَ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu kataba marsūman li-al-amīri Muḥammadi ibni Sulaymāna al-Zaynīyi wa-kāna nāʾiban fī Dimashqa
sentences.l: Then indeed-he wrote a-decree to-the-emir Muḥammad son-of Sulaymān the-Zaynī, and-was a-deputy in Damascus.
sentences.i: Then he wrote a decree to the emir Muḥammad son of Sulaymān al-Zaynī, who was viceroy in Damascus.

sentences.t: وَمَضْمُونُهُ أَنْ سَاعَةَ وُصُولِ الْمَرْسُومِ تَقْبِضَ عَلَى غَانِمِ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ وَتُرْسِلَهُ إِلَيَّ
sentences.tr: wa-maḍmūnuhu an sāʿata wuṣūli al-marsūmi taqbiḍa ʿalā Ghānimi ibni Ayyūba wa-tursilahu ilayya
sentences.l: And-its-purport: that [at] hour-of arrival-of the-decree you-seize upon Ghānim son-of Ayyūb and-send-him to-me.
sentences.i: Its purport was this: that at the very hour the decree arrived, he was to seize Ghānim son of Ayyūb and send him to me.
sentences.n: The print gives only ان, which I read as an with the subjunctive taqbiḍa, tursila (“that you seize … and send”). The caliph's own “to me” shows through the reported order.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا وَصَلَ الْمَرْسُومُ إِلَيْهِ قَبَّلَهُ وَوَضَعَهُ عَلَى رَأْسِهِ وَنَادَى فِى الْأَسْوَاقِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā waṣala al-marsūmu ilayhi qabbalahu wa-waḍaʿahu ʿalā raʾsihi wa-nādā fī al-aswāqi
sentences.l: And-when arrived the-decree to-him, he-kissed-it and-placed-it upon his-head, and-called-out in the-markets:
sentences.i: When the decree reached him he kissed it, laid it upon his head, and cried out in the markets:
sentences.n: Kissing the document and raising it to the head is the gesture of reverence owed to a sovereign's writ.

sentences.t: مَنْ أَرَادَانْ يَنْهَبَ فَعَلَيْهِ بِدَارِ غَانِمِ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ
sentences.tr: man arāda an yanhaba fa-ʿalayhi bi-dāri Ghānimi ibni Ayyūba
sentences.l: Whoever wished to plunder, then upon-him [be it] with-house-of Ghānim son-of Ayyūb.
sentences.i: Whoever wishes to plunder, let him make for the house of Ghānim son of Ayyūb!
sentences.n: The print runs arāda an (“wished to”) into one word. ʿalayhi bi- is an idiom of urging: “let him take himself to …”.

sentences.t: فَجَاءُوا إِلَى الدَّارِ فَوَجَدُوا أُمَّ غَانِمٍ وَأُخْتَهُ قَدْ صَنَعَتَا لَهُ قَبْرًا فِي وَسَطِ الدَّارِ وَقَعَدَتَا عِنْدَهُ تَبْكِيَانِ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-jāʾū ilā al-dāri fa-wajadū umma Ghānimin wa-ukhtahu qad ṣanaʿatā lahu qabran fī wasaṭi al-dāri wa-qaʿadatā ʿindahu tabkiyāni ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And-they-came to the-house and-found mother-of Ghānim and-his-sister, who-had made for-him a-tomb in middle-of the-house and-sat-down beside-it weeping(two) over-him.
sentences.i: They came to the house and found Ghānim's mother and his sister, who had made a tomb for him in the middle of the house and sat beside it, weeping for him.
sentences.n: ṣanaʿatā, qaʿadatā and tabkiyāni are dual feminine, for the two women. The tomb is a mourning-cenotaph, since he was supposed dead or lost.

sentences.t: فَمَسَكُوهُمَا وَنَهَبُوا الدَّارَ وَلَمْ تَعْلَمَا مَا الْخَبَرُ
sentences.tr: fa-masakūhumā wa-nahabū al-dāra wa-lam taʿlamā mā al-khabaru
sentences.l: And-they-seized-them-two and-plundered the-house, and-not they-two-knew what the-news.
sentences.i: They seized the two women and plundered the house, and the women had no notion what it was about.
sentences.n: Masaka for “seize” is the everyday Middle Arabic verb, replacing classical amsaka.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَحْضَرُوهُمَا عِنْدَ السُّلْطَانِ سَأَلَهُمَا مِنْ غَانِمٍ وَلَدِهِمَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aḥḍarūhumā ʿinda al-sulṭāni saʾalahumā min Ghānimin waladihimā
sentences.l: And-when they-brought-them-two before the-sultan, he-asked-them-two from Ghānim, their-two-son.
sentences.i: When they were brought before the sultan, he questioned them about Ghānim, their son.
sentences.n: I read min where classical Arabic would say ʿan (“asked about”). The print could also be read man, “who is Ghānim, their son?”; the sense of the answer fits “about”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتَا لَهُ مِنْ مُدَّةِ سَنَةٍ أَوْ أَكْثَرَ مَا وَقَفْنَا لَهُ عَلَى خَبَرٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qālatā lahu min muddati sanatin aw akthara mā waqafnā lahu ʿalā khabarin
sentences.l: And-they-two-said to-him: From a-span-of a-year or more not we-have-stood for-him upon news.
sentences.i: And they said to him: For a year or more we have had no news of him.
sentences.n: Waqafa ʿalā khabar is “to come upon (a piece of) news”.

sentences.t: فَرَدُّ وهُمَا إِلَى مَكَانِهِمَا هَذَا
sentences.tr: fa-raddū humā ilā makānihimā hādhā
sentences.l: And-they-sent-back them-two to their-two-place this.
sentences.i: And the two were sent back to the place where they lived.
sentences.n: The print divides فردوهما, fa-raddūhumā (“and they sent them back”), by a stray space after فرد. The “they” are the sultan's men.

sentences.t: أَمَّا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِهِمَا
sentences.tr: ammā kāna min amrihimā
sentences.l: As-for what-was of affair-of-them-two.
sentences.i: So much for those two.
sentences.n: The usual formula is أما ما كان من …; the print has only اما كان, so either the ما has merged into أَمَّا or it has dropped out. The formula closes one thread before the story turns to another.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَاكَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ غَانِمِ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ الْمُتَيَّمِ الْمَسْلُوبِ فَإِنَّهُ لَمَّا سُلِبَتْ نِعْمَتُهُ وَنَظَرَ إِلَى حَالِهِ فَبَكَى عَلَي نَفْسِهِ حَتَّى انْفَطَرَ قَلْبُهُ وَهَاجَ عَلَى وَجْهِهِ وَسَارَ إِلَى آخِرِ النَّهَارِ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā mākāna min amri Ghānimi ibni Ayyūba al-mutayyami al-maslūbi fa-innahu lammā sulibat niʿmatuhu wa-naẓara ilā ḥālihi fa-bakā ʿalā nafsihi ḥattā infaṭara qalbuhu wa-hāja ʿalā wajhihi wa-sāra ilā ākhiri al-nahāri
sentences.l: And-as-for what-was of affair-of Ghānim son-of Ayyūb, the-love-enthralled, the-despoiled: indeed-he, when was-taken-away his-bounty and-he-looked at his-state, wept over his-self until burst his-heart, and-surged upon his-face and-travelled to end-of the-day.
sentences.i: As for what befell Ghānim son of Ayyūb, the love-stricken, the despoiled: when his fortune was stripped from him and he looked upon his state, he wept over himself until his heart was near to bursting, then set off wandering at random, and walked on till the end of the day.
sentences.n: The print spells ʿalā as علي (with yā) in “over himself”; it is read ʿalā. Hāja ʿalā wajhihi is probably the idiom hāma ʿalā wajhihi, “wandered aimlessly”; hāja means “was stirred up, surged”, and the print's reading is kept. Al-mutayyam, “enthralled by love”, is a standing epithet of Ghānim.

sentences.t: وَقَدِ ازْدَادَ بِهِ الْجُوعُ وَأَضَرَّبِهِ الْمَشْيُ
sentences.tr: wa-qadi izdāda bihi al-jūʿu wa-aḍarra bihi al-mashyu
sentences.l: And-indeed grew in-him the-hunger, and-harmed-him the-walking.
sentences.i: His hunger had grown upon him, and the walking had worn him down.
sentences.n: The print runs aḍarra bihi (“harmed him”) into one word.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا وَصَلَ إِلَى بَلَدٍ دَخَلَهَا وَذَهَبَ إِلَى مَسْجِدٍ وَجَلَسَ عَلَى بُرْشٍ وَأَسْنَدَ ظَهْرَهُ إِلَى حَائِطِ الْمَسْجِدِ وَارْتَمَى وَهُوَ فِي غَايَةِ الْجُوعِ وَالتَّعَبِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā waṣala ilā baladin dakhalahā wa-dhahaba ilā masjidin wa-jalasa ʿalā burshin wa-asnada ẓahrahu ilā ḥāʾiṭi al-masjidi wa-irtamā wa-huwa fī ghāyati al-jūʿi wa-al-taʿabi
sentences.l: And-when he-arrived at a-town, he-entered-it and-went to a-mosque, and-sat upon a-mat, and-propped his-back to wall-of the-mosque, and-threw-himself-down, while-he in extremity-of the-hunger and-the-weariness.
sentences.i: When he came to a town he entered it, made for a mosque, sat down on a mat, propped his back against the mosque wall and sank down, in the last extremity of hunger and weariness.
sentences.n: Bursh (a mat or rug) is obscure to me; the vowel is my best guess, and the sense is clear from context.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَلْ مُقِيمًا هُنَاكَ إِلَى الصَّبَاحِ وَقَدْ خَفَقَ قَلْبُهُ مِنَ الْجُوعِ وَرَكِبَ عَلَى جِلْدِهِ الْقَمْلُ مِنَ الْعَرَقِ وَصَارَتْ رَائِحَتُهُ زَفِرَةً وَتَغَيَّرَتْ أَحْوَالُهُ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazal muqīman hunāka ilā al-ṣabāḥi wa-qad khafaqa qalbuhu min al-jūʿi wa-rakiba ʿalā jildihi al-qamlu min al-ʿaraqi wa-ṣārat rāʾiḥatuhu zafiratan wa-taghayyarat aḥwāluhu
sentences.l: And-not he-ceased staying there until the-morning, and-had throbbed his-heart from the-hunger, and-mounted upon his-skin the-lice from the-sweat, and-became his-smell foul, and-changed his-conditions.
sentences.i: He stayed there until morning, his heart fluttering from hunger; lice crept over his skin out of the sweat, his smell turned foul, and his whole condition changed.
sentences.n: I read zafira as “foul-smelling”; the print gives only زفرة, which could also be zafra, “a sigh”, but a stench suits the lice and sweat. Lam yazal muqīman is “he kept on staying”.

sentences.t: فَأَتَى أَهْلُ تِلْكَ الْبَلْدَةِ يُصَلُّونَ الصُّبْحَ فَوَجَدُوهُ مَطْرُوحًا ضَعِيفًا هَزِيلًا مِنَ الْجُوعِ وَعَلَيْهِ آثَارُ النِّعْمَةِ لَائِحَةً
sentences.tr: fa-atā ahlu tilka al-baldati yuṣallūna al-ṣubḥa fa-wajadūhu maṭrūḥan ḍaʿīfan hazīlan min al-jūʿi wa-ʿalayhi āthāru al-niʿmati lāʾiḥatan
sentences.l: And-came people-of that the-town praying the-dawn[-prayer], and-found-him thrown-down, weak, emaciated from the-hunger, and-upon-him traces-of the-comfort visible.
sentences.i: Then the people of that town came to say the dawn prayer, and found him cast down, weak and wasted with hunger, though the marks of former ease were still plain upon him.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا صَلَّوْا وَأَقْبَلُوا عَلَيْهِ وَجَدُوهُ بَرْدَانًا جَائِعًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ṣallaw wa-aqbalū ʿalayhi wajadūhu bardānan jāʾiʿan
sentences.l: And-when they-prayed and-turned upon-him, they-found-him cold, hungry.
sentences.i: When they had prayed and turned to him, they found him cold and hungry.
sentences.n: Bardān (“feeling cold”) is properly a diptote (bardāna); the print's alif of tanwīn, bardānan, is the common loosening.

sentences.t: فَأَعْطَوْهُ ثَوْبًا عَتِيقًا قَدْ بَلِيَتْ أَكْمَامُهُ وَقَالُوا لَهُ يَاغَرِيبُ مِنْ أَيْنَ تَكُونُ وَمَا سَبَبُ ضَعْفِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-aʿṭawhu thawban ʿatīqan qad baliyat akmāmuhu wa-qālū lahu yāgharību min ayna takūnu wa-mā sababu ḍaʿfika
sentences.l: And-they-gave-him a-garment old, had worn-out its-sleeves, and-they-said to-him: O-stranger, from where you-are, and-what the-cause-of your-weakness?
sentences.i: They gave him an old garment with worn-out sleeves, and said to him: Stranger, where do you come from, and what has made you so weak?
sentences.n: The print joins the vocative to its noun: yā-gharīb. Min ayna takūn, literally “from where are you”, is the ordinary way to ask where someone is from.

sentences.t: فَفَتَحَ عَيْنَيْهِ فِيهِمْ وَبَكَى وَلَمْ يَرُدَّ عَلَيْهِمْ جَوَابًا
sentences.tr: fa-fataḥa ʿaynayhi fīhim wa-bakā wa-lam yarudda ʿalayhim jawāban
sentences.l: And-he-opened his-two-eyes upon-them and-wept, and-not he-returned to-them an-answer.
sentences.i: He opened his eyes upon them and wept, and gave them no answer.

sentences.t: فَذَهَبَ أَحَدُهُمْ وَقَدْ عَرَفَ أَنَّهُ جَيْعَانُ فَأَتَى لَهُ بِسُكُرُّجَةِ عَسَلٍ وَرَغِيفَيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-dhahaba aḥaduhum wa-qad ʿarafa annahu jayʿānu fa-atā lahu bi-sukurrujati ʿasalin wa-raghīfayni
sentences.l: And-went one-of-them, and-he-had known that-he hungry, and-came for-him with-a-saucer-of honey and-two-loaves.
sentences.i: One of them went off, having understood that the man was hungry, and brought him a small dish of honey and two loaves.
sentences.n: Jayʿān is the Middle Arabic form of classical jawʿān, “hungry”. Atā lahu bi- is “brought him …”, literally “came for him with …”.

sentences.t: فَأَكَلَ يَسِيرًا وَقَعَدُوا عِنْدَهُ حَتَّى طَلَعَتِ الشَّمْسُ وَانْصَرَفُوا لِأَ شْغَا لِهِمْ
sentences.tr: fa-akala yasīran wa-qaʿadū ʿindahu ḥattā ṭalaʿati al-shamsu wa-inṣarafū li-ashghālihim
sentences.l: And-he-ate a-little, and-they-sat by-him until rose the-sun, and-departed to-their-occupations.
sentences.i: He ate a little, and they sat beside him until the sun rose, and then went away about their business.
sentences.n: The print breaks لأشغالهم into three pieces, لا شغا لهم; it is read li-ashghālihim, “to their occupations”. In the pointed text the pieces are li-a, shghā, lihim.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَلْ عَلَى هَذَا الْحَالِ شَهْرًا وَهُوَ عِنْدَهُمْ وَقَدْ تَزَايَدَ بِهِ الضَّعْفُ وَالْمَرَضُ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazal ʿalā hādhā al-ḥāli shahran wa-huwa ʿindahum wa-qad tazāyada bihi al-ḍaʿfu wa-al-maraḍu
sentences.l: And-not he-ceased upon this the-state a-month, while-he with-them, and-had increased in-him the-weakness and-the-sickness.
sentences.i: So he remained in that state for a month, living among them, while weakness and sickness grew upon him.
sentences.n: Ḥāl (“state”) is treated as masculine here, hādhā al-ḥāl.

sentences.t: فَبَكَوْا عَلَيْهِ وَتَعَطَّفُوا وَتَشَاوَرُوا مَعَ بَعْضِهِمْ فِي أَمْرِهِ فَاتَّفَقُوا فِي أَنَّهُمْ أَنْ يُوصِلُوهُ إِلَى الْمَارَسْتَانِ الَّذِي بِبَغْدَادَ
sentences.tr: fa-bakaw ʿalayhi wa-taʿaṭṭafū wa-tashāwarū maʿa baʿḍihim fī amrihi fa-ittafaqū fī annahum an yūṣilūhu ilā al-mārastāni alladhī bi-Baghdāda
sentences.l: And-they-wept over-him and-showed-tenderness and-took-counsel with some-of-them about his-affair, and-agreed on that-they that they-convey-him to the-hospital which in-Baghdad.
sentences.i: They wept over him and were moved to pity, and took counsel together about his case; and they agreed to carry him to the hospital in Baghdad,
sentences.n: The print has both أنهم and أن (“that they — that they convey him”), a doubled conjunction; it reads smoothly as one “that”. Al-māristān is the Persian-derived word for a hospital.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَاهُمْ كَذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamāhum ka-dhālika
sentences.l: And-while-they thus,
sentences.i: And while they were thus engaged …
sentences.n: This fragment continues into the next slice: the main clause of “while they were thus …” follows there.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِامْرَأَتَيْنِ شَحَّاذَتَيْنِ دَخَلَتَا عَلَيْهِ وَكَانَتَا هَؤُلَاءِ أُمَّهُ وَأُخْتَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-imraʾatayni shaḥḥādhatayni dakhalatā ʿalayhi wa-kānatā hāʾulāʾi ummahu wa-ukhtahu
sentences.l: And-behold, with-two-women, two-beggars, they-two-entered upon-him, and-they-two-were these: his-mother and-his-sister.
sentences.i: And behold, two beggar women came in to him; and they were none other than his mother and his sister.
sentences.n: This slice opens mid-sentence: the clause continues from the neighbouring slice before it. Here هؤلاء, properly “these” (plural), points at the two women, with “his mother and his sister” following in apposition.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآهُمَا أَعْطَاهُمَا الْخُبْزَ الَّذِي عِنْدَ رَأْسِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾāhumā aʿṭāhumā al-khubza alladhī ʿinda raʾsihi
sentences.l: And-when he-saw-the-two-of-them, he-gave-the-two-of-them the-bread which at his-head,
sentences.i: When he saw them, he gave them the bread that lay beside his head,

sentences.t: وَنَامَتَا عِنْدَهُ تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةَ وَلَمْ يَعْرِفْهُمَا
sentences.tr: wa-nāmatā ʿindahu tilka al-layla wa-lam yaʿrifhumā
sentences.l: and-they-two-slept at-him that the-night, and-not he-knew-the-two-of-them.
sentences.i: and the two slept beside him that night, and he did not know them.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَ ثَانِيَ يَوْمٍ أَتَاهُ أَهْلُ الْقَرْيَةِ وَأَحْضَرُوا لَهُ جَمَلًا وَقَالُوا لِلْجَمَّالِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kāna thāniya yawmin atāhu ahlu al-qaryati wa-aḥḍarū lahu jamalan wa-qālū li-al-jammāli
sentences.l: And-when it-was second-of day, came-to-him the-people-of the-village, and-brought for-him a-camel, and-said to-the-camel-man:
sentences.i: When the next day came, the people of the village went to him, brought a camel for him, and said to the camel-driver:
sentences.n: ثاني يوم, “second day”, is the ordinary idiom for “the next day”; the first noun stands in construct with the second.

sentences.t: اِحْمِلْ هَذَا الْمَرِيضَ فَوْقَ الْجَمَلِ
sentences.tr: iḥmil hādhā al-marīḍa fawqa al-jamali
sentences.l: Carry this the-sick-one above the-camel,
sentences.i: Lift this sick man upon the camel,

sentences.t: فَإِذَا وَصَلْتَ إِلَى بَغْدَادَ فَإِنَّكَ تَحُطُّهُ فِي بَابِ الْمَارِسْتَانِ لَعَلَّهُ يَتَدَاوَى وَيَتَعَانَى وَيَبْقَى لَكَ الْأَجْرُ
sentences.tr: fa-idhā waṣalta ilā Baghdāda fa-innaka taḥuṭṭuhu fī bābi al-mārisitāni laʿallahu yatadāwā wa-yataʿānā wa-yabqā laka al-ajru
sentences.l: then-if you-arrive to Baghdād, then-indeed-you you-set-him-down in gate-of the-hospital, perhaps-he he-is-treated and-is-tended and-remains for-you the-reward.
sentences.i: and when you reach Baghdad, set him down at the gate of the hospital, that he may be treated and tended, and the reward may remain yours.
sentences.n: المارستان is the Persian-derived word for a hospital. يتعانى is obscure: I take it as “is cared for, mends” (perhaps meant for يتعافى, “recovers”); the print gives only the letters we have.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُمُ السَّمْعُ وَالطَّاعَةُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahumu al-samʿu wa-al-ṭāʿatu
sentences.l: So-he-said to-them: the-hearing and-the-obedience.
sentences.i: So he said to them: With hearing and obedience.
sentences.n: The print omits the bi- of the formula; it stands as a bare elliptical phrase, nominative, which I vocalise as printed.

sentences.t: فَبَعْدَ ذَلِكَ أَخْرَجُوا غَانِمَ بْنَ أَيُّوبَ مِنَ الْمَسْجِدِ وَحَمَلُوهُ بِالْبَرْشِ الَّذِي هُوَ نَائِمٌ عَلَيْهِ فَوْقَ الْجَمَلِ
sentences.tr: fa-baʿda dhālika akhrajū Ghānima ibna Ayyūba mina al-masjidi wa-ḥamalūhu bi-al-barshi alladhī huwa nāʾimun ʿalayhi fawqa al-jamali
sentences.l: So-after that they-brought-out Ghānim son-of Ayyūb from the-mosque, and-carried-him with-the-mat which he asleep upon-it, above the-camel.
sentences.i: After that they brought Ghānim son of Ayyūb out of the mosque and lifted him, mat and all, upon the camel, lying as he was.
sentences.n: I read البرش as barsh, “mat”, by the sense; the word is rare and the pointing is a guess. The relative clause الذي هو نائم عليه, “on which he is asleep”, spells out the pronoun هو, a Middle Arabic habit.

sentences.t: وَجَاتْ أُمُّهُ وَأُخْتُهُ يَتَفَرَّجَانِ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ جُمْلَةِ النَّاسِ وَلَمْ تَعْلَمَابِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-jāt ummuhu wa-ukhtuhu yatafarrajāni ʿalayhi min jumlati al-nāsi wa-lam taʿlamā bihi
sentences.l: And-came his-mother and-his-sister, the-two watching upon-him, from the-sum-of the-people, and-not they-two-knew of-him.
sentences.i: His mother and his sister came and watched him among the crowd, and did not know him.
sentences.n: وجات is the print’s spelling of وجاءت (jāʾat), without hamza; the unpointed form is simply what it says. Note too يتفرجان, the masculine dual, for two women. تعلمابه is printed as a single word, تعلما به, “they knew of him”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمَا نَظَرَتَا إِلَيْهِ وَتَأَمَّلَتَاهُ وَقَالَتَا إِنَّهُ شَبِيهٌ لِغَانِمٍ ابْنِنَا
sentences.tr: thumma innahumā naẓaratā ilayhi wa-taʾammalatāhu wa-qālatā innahu shabīhun li-Ghānimin ibninā
sentences.l: Then indeed-the-two-of-them looked-two at-him and-examined-him-two, and-said-two: Indeed-he like to-Ghānim our-son,
sentences.i: Then the two looked at him and studied him, and said: He is the very likeness of Ghānim, our son;

sentences.t: فَيَاتُرَى هَلْ هُوَ هَذَا الضَّعِيفُ أَوْلَا
sentences.tr: fa-yāturā hal huwa hādhā al-ḍaʿīfu awlā
sentences.l: so-O-it-is-seen: is he this the-feeble-one, or not?
sentences.i: so one wonders: can this feeble wretch be he, or not?
sentences.n: ياترى, here printed joined to the fa-, is the colloquial “I wonder”, literally something like “O, it is seen”.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا غَانِمٌ فَإِنَّهُ مَا أَفَاقَ إِلَّا وَهُوَ مَحْمُولٌ عَلَى الْجَمَلِ مَشْدُودٌ بِحَبْلٍ فَبَكَى وَاشْتَكَى
sentences.tr: wa-ammā Ghānimun fa-innahu mā afāqa illā wa-huwa maḥmūlun ʿalā al-jamali mashdūdun bi-ḥablin fa-bakā wa-ishtakā
sentences.l: And-as-for Ghānim, indeed-he not he-recovered-consciousness except while-he carried on the-camel, bound with-a-rope; so-he-wept and-complained.
sentences.i: As for Ghānim, he came to himself only when he was already being carried on the camel, bound with a rope; and he wept and moaned.

sentences.t: وَأَهْلُ الْقَرْيَهْ يَنْظُرُونَ أُمَّهُ وَأُخْتَهُ تَبْكِيَانِ عَلَيْهِ وَلَمْ تَعْرِفَابِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-ahlu al-qaryah yanẓurūna ummahu wa-ukhtahu tabkiyāni ʿalayhi wa-lam taʿrifā bihi
sentences.l: and-the-people-of the-village looking-at his-mother and-his-sister, the-two weeping over-him, and-not they-two-knew of-him.
sentences.i: while the villagers looked on at his mother and his sister weeping over him; and they did not recognise him.
sentences.n: القريه is printed with final ه for ة; I read it as the pausal -ah, with no case ending. Again تعرفابه is one printed word, تعرفا به.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ سَافَرَتْ أُمُّهُ وَأُخْتُهُ إِلَى أَنْ وَصَلْنَا إِلَى بَغْدَادَ
sentences.tr: thumma sāfarat ummuhu wa-ukhtuhu ilā an waṣalnā ilā Baghdāda
sentences.l: Then travelled his-mother and-his-sister until that we-arrived to Baghdād.
sentences.i: Then his mother and his sister journeyed on until we reached Baghdad.
sentences.n: The print has the first person, وصلنا, “we arrived”, in the middle of third-person narrative; it may be a slip for وصلتا, but I vocalise what is printed.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا الْجَمَّالُ فَمَازَالَ سَائِرًابِهِ حَتَّى حَطَّهُ عَلَى بَابِ الْمَارِسْتَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā al-jammālu fa-mā zāla sāʾiran bihi ḥattā ḥaṭṭahu ʿalā bābi al-mārisitāni
sentences.l: And-as-for the-camel-man, so-he-ceased-not going with-him until he-set-him-down upon gate-of the-hospital
sentences.i: As for the camel-driver, he went steadily on with him until he set him down at the gate of the hospital,
sentences.n: ما زال ... سائرا به, “he did not cease going with him”, is printed with the words run together: فمازال, سائرابه.

sentences.t: وَأَخَذَ جَمَلَهُ وَذَهَبَ
sentences.tr: wa-akhadha jamalahu wa-dhahaba
sentences.l: and-took his-camel and-went.
sentences.i: and took his camel and went away.

sentences.t: فَتَمَّ غَانِمٌ رَاقِدًا هُنَاكَ إِلَى الصَّبَاحِ
sentences.tr: fa-tamma Ghānimun rāqidan hunāka ilā al-ṣabāḥi
sentences.l: So-remained Ghānim lying there until the-morning.
sentences.i: So Ghānim lay there until morning.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا انْدَرَجَتِ النَّاسُ فِى الطَّرِيقِ نَظَرُوا إِلَيْهِ وَقَدْ صَارَرِقَّ الْخِلَالِ وَالنَّاسُ يَتَفَرَّجُونَ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā indarajati al-nāsu fī al-ṭarīqi naẓarū ilayhi wa-qad ṣāra riqqa al-khilāli wa-al-nāsu yatafarrajūna ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And-when went-about the-people in the-road, they-looked at-him, and-already he-had-become thinness-of the-interstices, while-the-people watching upon-him.
sentences.i: When the people began to stir about the road, they saw him, wasted and wretched, and the people stood gazing at him.
sentences.n: اندرجت الناس: the feminine singular verb with الناس is Middle Arabic agreement, and اندرج, “went about, set out”, is my best reading. صاررق الخلال is printed run together and is obscure: I take it as صار رِقَّ الخلال, “had grown thin of body”, but الخلال may be a slip for الحال, “thin of state”, i.e. in a pitiable condition. The sense either way is wasted and wretched.

sentences.t: فَجَاءَ شَيْخُ السُّوقِ وَأَزَاحَ النَّاسَ عَنْهُ وَقَٰلَ
sentences.tr: fa-jāʾa shaykhu al-sūqi wa-azāḥa al-nāsa ʿanhu wa-qāla
sentences.l: So-came the-elder-of the-market and-removed the-people from-him, and-said:
sentences.i: Then the headman of the market came, drove the people back from him, and said:
sentences.n: وقل is the print’s slip for وقال, so it is pointed with the dagger alif. شيخ السوق is the head of the market guild.

sentences.t: أَنَا أَكْسِبُ الْجَنَّةَ بِهَذَا الْمِسْكِينِ
sentences.tr: anā aksibu al-jannata bi-hādhā al-miskīni
sentences.l: I I-earn the-garden by-this the-poor-one;
sentences.i: I shall win Paradise through this poor wretch;

sentences.t: فَإِنَّهُمْ مَتَى أَدْخَلُوهُ الْمَارِسْتَانَ قَتَلُوهُ فِي يَوْمٍ وَاحِدٍ
sentences.tr: fa-innahum matā adkhalūhu al-mārisitāna qatalūhu fī yawmin wāḥidin
sentences.l: for-indeed-they, whenever they-put-him-in the-hospital, they-killed-him in one day.
sentences.i: for the moment they put him in the hospital they will kill him within a day.
sentences.n: Both verbs are perfects, but after متى they carry a conditional, present or future sense.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَمَرَ صِبْيَانَهُ بِحَمْلِهِ فَحَمَلُوهُ إِلَى بَيْتِهِ وَفَرَشَ لَهُ فَرْشًا جَدِيدًا وَوَضَعَ لَهُ مِخَدَّةً جَدِيدَةً
sentences.tr: thumma amara ṣibyānahu bi-ḥamlihi fa-ḥamalūhu ilā baytihi wa-farasha lahu farshan jadīdan wa-waḍaʿa lahu mikhaddatan jadīdatan
sentences.l: Then he-commanded his-boys with-carrying-him, and-they-carried-him to his-house, and-spread for-him a-spread new, and-placed for-him a-cushion new.
sentences.i: Then he ordered his lads to carry him, and they carried him to his house; he spread fresh bedding for him and laid a new cushion for him.
sentences.n: أمر بـ, “command to do”, takes bi- for the thing commanded: here “with his carrying”.

sentences.t: وَقَٰلَ لِزَوْجَتِهِ اِخْدِمِيهِ بِنُصْحٍ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla li-zawjatihi ikhdimīhi bi-nuṣḥin
sentences.l: And-said to-his-wife: Serve-him with-sincerity!
sentences.i: And he said to his wife: Wait upon him with true care.
sentences.n: Again وقل for وقال.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ طَيِّبْ عَلَى الرَّأْسِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat ṭayyib ʿalā al-raʾsi
sentences.l: So-she-said: Good, upon the-head.
sentences.i: She said: Very well, upon my head.
sentences.n: طيب is the colloquial “very well”, and على الرأس, “upon the head”, is a courteous formula of willing assent.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تَشَمَّرَتْ وَسَخَّنَتْ مَاءً وَغَسَلَتْ يَدَيْهِ وَرِجْلَيْهِ وَبَدَنَهُ وَأَلْبَسَتْهُ ثَوْبًا مِنْ لُبْسِ جَوَارِيهَا
sentences.tr: thumma tashammarat wa-sakhkhanat māʾan wa-ghasalat yadayhi wa-rijlayhi wa-badanahu wa-albasathu thawban min lubsi jawārīhā
sentences.l: Then she-tucked-up-her-sleeves, and-heated water, and-washed his-two-hands and-his-two-feet and-his-body, and-clothed-him a-garment from the-clothing-of her-slave-girls.
sentences.i: Then she girded herself, heated water, washed his hands, his feet and his body, and clothed him in a robe from her slave-girls’ wardrobe.
sentences.n: لبس, here “clothing, garments”, is pointed lubs by the sense.

sentences.t: وَأَسْقَتْهُ قَدَحَ شَرَابٍ وَرَشَّتْ عَلَيْهِ مَاءَ وَرْدٍ فَأَفَاقَ وَاشْتَكَى
sentences.tr: wa-asqathu qadaḥa sharābin wa-rashshat ʿalayhi māʾa wardin fa-afāqa wa-ishtakā
sentences.l: And-she-gave-him-to-drink a-cup-of drink, and-sprinkled upon-him water-of rose, and-he-recovered and-complained.
sentences.i: She gave him a cup of sherbet to drink and sprinkled him with rose-water; and he revived and moaned.

sentences.t: وَافْتَكَرَ مَحْبُوبَتَهُ قُوتَ الْقُلُوبِ فَزَادَتْ بِهِ الْكُرُوبُ
sentences.tr: wa-iftakara maḥbūbatahu Qūta al-Qulūbi fa-zādat bihi al-kurūbu
sentences.l: and-remembered his-beloved Qūt al-Qulūb, so-increased with-him the-griefs.
sentences.i: and he remembered his beloved Qūt al-Qulūb, and his sorrows grew upon him.
sentences.n: The two clauses end on the rhyme -ūb, الْقُلُوب and الكروب. Here زاد بـ means “grew upon, came heavier on”.

sentences.t: هَذَا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ
sentences.tr: hādhā mā kāna min amrihi
sentences.l: This what was from his-affair.
sentences.i: So much for his affair.
sentences.n: A stock transition formula: “this is what befell him”.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَاكَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ قُوتِ الْقُلُوبِ فَإِنَّهُ لَمَّا غَضِبَ عَلَيْهَا الْخَلِيفَةُ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā mākāna min amri Qūti al-Qulūbi fa-innahu lammā ghaḍiba ʿalayhā al-khalīfatu
sentences.l: And-as-for what was from affair-of Qūt al-Qulūb: indeed-it, when was-angry upon-her the-caliph,
sentences.i: But as for what befell Qūt al-Qulūb: when the Caliph grew angry with her,
sentences.n: The print runs ما كان together as one word. The sentence breaks off here and continues in the neighbouring slice after it. The anticipatory pronoun in فإنه, “indeed it”, looks ahead to the clause that follows.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And-overtook Shahrazād the-morning, and-she-fell-silent from the-speech the-permitted.
sentences.i: And morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
sentences.n: The closing formula, in rhyme: الصباح / المباح, “the morning / the permitted”. “Permitted speech” is the stock phrase for the tale she is allowed to tell.
